prompt:
I need the front end for Driftfield. A spatial explorer of a speech-recognition company's training and evaluation audio, where every clip is placed by acoustic and linguistic similarity, used by the data team during its weekly review in a shared room.

Who's using it: Priyanka Oyelaran, lead of the data-quality team, at the large display in the team's review room with five annotators and an ML engineer around her. She's steering the session while others call out regions to look at. They all know speech data well, and some know the model internals.

What they're doing right now: Last Thursday's model release got worse on accented English in noisy settings, and today's review is to find where in the data that's happening. Priyanka is moving through the similarity space: zooming toward a dense region where new failing evaluation clips have piled up next to a sparse patch of training data, comparing it with a nearby healthy region, and playing sample clips aloud for the room. By the end of the hour the group needs to agree on a bounded region to send for relabeling and targeted collection, and to name it so the work can be tracked.

What's in the system at this point: 1.8 million training clips and 64,000 evaluation clips, each with 2D and 3D projected coordinates, duration (1–30 s), language and accent label, recording environment (car, street, call center, quiet room), signal-to-noise ratio, transcript, model word error rate for releases v41 and v42, labeling vendor, and label confidence. 212 automatically found clusters with sizes and mean error. Flagged area: about 3,400 eval clips, Nigerian and Ghanaian English in street noise, WER up from 14% to 23% between releases, next to only 9,000 training clips. Seven saved regions from earlier reviews, such as 'Car-kit Spanish' (closed) and 'Overlapping speakers' (in relabeling), each with owner and status.

Build it as a working web app, opened in the state that person would see at that moment. No backend: use realistic mock data (no lorem ipsum, no placeholder names), and make the interactive parts actually work client-side.

Use whatever framework and tooling you like. When you're done there must be a static production build in ./out with ./out/index.html as the entry point. It will be served from the root of a plain static file server (no rewrites, no server code) and viewed in a desktop browser at 1440×900.
